file.content:
# Message List

## Concept

### Pitch

The chat history of prompt mode: the prompts sent to the harness and its responses, as a conversation.

### Shape

#### Description

Conversation-style, shows send prompts on the right, received input on the left.

#### Sent Prompt

A sent prompt shows the compiled markdown that was actually sent to the harness, rendered as markdown, once it has compiled. Its message header shows the name of the hidden anchor it was compiled from.

#### Response

A response from the harness is grouped by general type, in the order it happened. The harness's own text is shown as markdown. Tool calls in a row that share a general type (reading and searching files, editing files, running commands, the web, agents, and anything else) are gathered into one group, headed by that type and how many calls it holds. Each call in a group lists the tool's name, its most telling argument, and whether it is running, done, or failed, spelled out rather than only coloured.

#### Queue Background

The header along the top of the message list, holding the pinned prompt and the queue, has the same background colour as the tab bar.

#### Legibility

The output from a realtime agent should be readable and meaningful.  Make sure the font size is large enough, that the colours are legible.

use /lib

export scope MessageList:
    concept: {MessageListConcept}

concept MessageListConcept:
    pitch:
        The chat history of prompt mode: the prompts sent to the harness and
        its responses, as a conversation.

    shape: {MessageListShape}

shape MessageListShape:
    description:
        Conversation-style, shows send prompts on the right, received input on
        the left.

    sentPrompt:
        A sent prompt shows the compiled markdown that was actually sent to the
        harness, rendered as markdown, once it has compiled. Its message
        header shows the name of the hidden anchor it was compiled from.

    response:
        A response from the harness is grouped by general type, in the order it
        happened. The harness's own text is shown as markdown. Tool calls in a
        row that share a general type (reading and searching files, editing
        files, running commands, the web, agents, and anything else) are
        gathered into one group, headed by that type and how many calls it
        holds. Each call in a group lists the tool's name, its most telling
        argument, and whether it is running, done, or failed, spelled out
        rather than only coloured.

    queueBackground:
        The header along the top of the message list, holding the pinned prompt
        and the queue, has the same background colour as the tab bar.

    legibility:
        The output from a realtime agent should be readable and
        meaningful.  Make sure the font size is large enough, that the colours
        are legible.

content.text:
I added the loading skeleton to the message list. While a task is still running, the output table now ends with a placeholder row, and each part of that row turns real as soon as the harness says what it is. The prompt-mode tests (13) and clippy pass. In the full suite, 80 of 81 pass. The one failure is `palette::tests::lists_files_by_path_leaving_out_ignored_ones`, and I don't think this change caused it. It fails the same way every run, and it tests the palette's file list, which doesn't use this table. The list it gets back leaves out `.claude/skills/x/SKILL.md`, which I'd guess is a global gitignore on your machine hiding `.claude`, but I didn't check.

**How a row fills in** (all in `src/prompt_mode.rs`):
- **Nothing known yet:** the row is all skeleton, both the type badge and two text lines. This row is there from the moment a task starts, which replaces the old "Waiting for the harness…" spinner.
- **The harness starts replying:** the badge turns into a real "Reply" badge, with skeleton lines beside it until the first words arrive.
- **A tool call starts:** the badge and the tool's name are real, and a skeleton bar stands in for its argument until that arrives. The status column already shows "running".
- **The row is complete** (words have arrived, or the tool's argument is known): a fresh skeleton row appears below for whatever comes next.
- **The task finishes:** no skeleton rows are left. A task that produced nothing shows "No output."

The palette's search results use the same table, so they get the skeleton too. I added a test, `unfinished_reply_ends_in_a_row_still_filling_in`, that walks through these steps.

**One quirk:** some tools never send an argument we can summarise. Those keep the skeleton bar until the call finishes.

I didn't edit the spec. If you want it to match, the "response" section in `spec/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.pi` would need a sentence about this skeleton row.
